summary.oneLiner: NephroPlus (Nephrocare Health Services Limited) is India's and Asia's largest dialysis network and the world's fifth largest by treatment volume, operating 520+ clinics across five countries.
summary.business: NephroPlus offers comprehensive dialysis care through a network of clinics, from diagnosis to treatment and wellness, including hemodialysis, home and mobile dialysis, supported by pharmacy, diagnostics, renal nutrition counseling and mental-health support. It reaches guests through in-hospital captive clinics, standalone clinics and government-backed public-private partnerships (PPP) across India, Nepal, the Philippines, Uzbekistan and Saudi Arabia (via a JV).

currentContext.expansion: NephroPlus grows via three routes: greenfield clinics (average 5 beds, first-year run rate ~250 treatments), brownfield unit-by-unit roll-up (lower upfront investment, faster ramp-up, average ~10 beds leveraging an existing guest base and local staff), and acquisitions (network roll-up). Acquired clinics typically reach operational breakeven in three to four months versus roughly twelve months for a greenfield clinic. themes.title: Hospitals, diagnostics & domestic healthcare
themes.need: Under-bedded India plus insurance penetration and preventive-care adoption drive a domestic healthcare capex + volume cycle distinct from export pharma. MAXHEALTH adding ~2,500+ beds (Gurgaon 500-bed by FY27); APOLLOHOSP/MEDANTA/KIMS/NH/ASTERDM/MAXHEALTH on hospitals; LALPATHLAB/METROPOLIS/THYROCARE/VIJAYA on diagnostics (LALPATHLAB guides 13-15% FY27); MEDPLUS/ENTERO on pharmacy/distribution; POLYMED on devices. The same India-only demand engine now also carries India-facing branded pharma, which is driven by domestic volume and price rather than the export book: GLAXO delivered its first INR 1,000cr quarter with 8.1% revenue growth, Shingrix at a ~INR 75cr annual run-rate (CY25, +80% YoY) and Jemperli's first-line approval expanding eligible patients from 800 to 6,000; ERIS (dermatology 15% of revenue after INR 1,265cr of domestic brand acquisitions), SANOFI (India-for-India, NLEM price cuts) and THEMISMED (hospital segment +20% YoY) sit on the same axis.
themes.driver: New-bed commissioning + occupancy ramp; Tier 3/4 diagnostics penetration; CGHS rate revision; preventive-test volumes; domestic branded-formulation volume growth and NLEM/price actions.

hero.oneLiner: NephroPlus (Nephrocare Health Services Limited) is India's and Asia's largest dialysis network and the world's fifth largest by treatment volume, operating 520+ clinics across five countries.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: NephroPlus (Nephrocare Health Services Limited) is India's and Asia's largest dialysis network and the world's fifth largest by treatment volume, operating 520+ clinics across five countries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: NephroPlus offers comprehensive dialysis care through a network of clinics spanning diagnosis, treatment and wellness programs, including haemodialysis, home and mobile dialysis, supported by pharmacy. It operates in-hospital captive clinics, standalone clinics and government PPP formats across India and internationally (Philippines, Uzbekistan, Nepal), serving patients with End Stage Renal Disorder.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Kamal D. Shah — Co-founder: On dialysis for over 28 years; drives patient-centric focus
- Nephro Care India Limited — Similarly-named listed company: No connection; risk factor flags name similarity
- NephroPlus Foundation — Group foundation: Offers free/low-cost dialysis to underprivileged patients

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Core dialysis:** Haemodialysis, Home haemodialysis, Hemodiafiltration, Continuous renal replacement therapy, Plasmapheresis
- **Off-clinic / accessibility:** Holiday dialysis, Dialysis on call, Dialysis on wheels
- **Ancillary:** Pharmacy / dialysis-related pharmacy products, Renova dialyzer reprocessing system, RenAssure protocols, Enpidia training academy

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India
- Nepal
- Philippines
- Uzbekistan
- Saudi Arabia (Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, via JV)

certifications.title: Certs (RHP)
certifications.body:
- ISO 9001:2015
- JCI (Joint Commission International) accreditation — 31 clinics
- NABH (National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers) accreditation — 1491 clinics

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Centralized procurement of consumables and pharmaceuticals across clinics for uniform pricing and improved margins. Backward/vertical integration into key consumables: contract manufacturing arrangements for acid/bicarbonate (directly procures raw materials) and blood tubing sets (invested in proprietary moulds, sources tubing independently, engages contract manufacturers for assembly). Consumables as % of revenue fell from 32.59% (FY23) to 23.05% (H1FY26).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Expansion of clinic network and treatment volumes drives revenue
- Recurring revenue from chronic, life-sustaining nature of dialysis
- Consumables cost reduction (from 32.59% of revenue FY23 to 23.05% in H1FY26) improving margins
- Rising share of international revenue (11.70% FY23 to 31.79% FY25) at higher price points
- Operating leverage from scale in procurement and utilisation (utilisation rate 68.63% FY23 to 74.99% H1FY26)
- Faster breakeven for captive/brownfield (3-4 months) vs greenfield (12 months)

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Continue to consolidate leadership position in India by opening new clinics (167 new clinics via IPO proceeds)
- Selectively pursue strategic acquisitions and investments in Philippines, Uzbekistan and other key markets
- Deepen patient reach and geographic footprint in India, Philippines, Nepal and Uzbekistan
- Expand off-clinic and premium value-added services
- Drive cost efficiencies via centralized procurement and vertical integration of consumables

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Company intends to open 167 new dialysis clinics in India (69 greenfield, 98 brownfield) across ~0.19 million sq ft, funded partly by IPO net proceeds (Rs 1,291.06 million), over Fiscals 2026-2028, targeting states including Rajasthan, UP, Delhi, Telangana, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and others. Internationally, it plans to continue inorganic expansion in the Philippines and Uzbekistan and grow via the KSA joint venture. It scaled from 1 clinic in 2010 to 519 clinics by Sep 30, 2025.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- India's and Asia's largest dialysis chain; over 50% share of India's organized dialysis market (treatments), ~4.4x next largest provider (FY24 revenue)
- Only Indian dialysis provider scaled internationally; 519 clinics across 4 countries
- Scalable, asset-light, capital-efficient model (52.41% clinics on revenue-sharing)
- Protocol-led clinical excellence (RenAssure), proprietary tech (Renova, patient apps), Enpidia training academy
- Proven acquisition and integration track record (18 companies acquired)
- Patient-centric leadership backed by marquee PE/VC investors

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Captive clinic contract dependence — Captive clinics were 43.30% of revenue FY25 (62.23% FY23); cancellation/non-renewal of hospital arrangements could materially hurt revenue
- Reimbursement / regulated pricing — Prices depend on recommended/mandatory fees; Philippine and Uzbekistan reimbursement frameworks subject to periodic revision
- Acquisition and integration risk — Growth relies on acquisitions (18 done); integration failures could hurt returns; some subsidiaries loss-making
- Geographic concentration — Substantial revenue from southern India clinics; international ops carry FX and regulatory exposure
- Key personnel / promoter concentration — Dependence on founder Vikram Vuppala; corporate promoters lack line-of-business experience
- Accreditation dependence — Loss of NABH/JCI/PhilHealth accreditation could impact revenue
- Third-party payer / receivables risk — Financial difficulties of payers may cause payment delays or write-offs
- Regulatory / FEMA compliance — Past delays in RBI/FEMA filings; extensive licensing requirements

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Open 167 new dialysis clinics in India (69 greenfield, 98 brownfield) funded from net proceeds**
- **Deploy Rs 1,291.06 million net proceeds on India clinic capex over FY26-FY28**
- **Prepay/repay Rs 1,359.99 million of borrowings in FY2026**
- **Continue selective strategic acquisitions in Philippines, Uzbekistan and other key markets**
- **Deliver dialysis care for minimum 1,100 patients/year under 10-year Uzbekistan PPP tender**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Three growth levers: steady ramp-up at existing clinics, roll-ups of clinics in countries where NephroPlus already operates, and entry into new countries or sizeable acquisitions.
- Continue expanding the dialysis network, enhance clinical excellence, invest in technology and digital healthcare solutions, strengthen the talent pool, and pursue strategic growth opportunities across India and selected international markets.
